display_name: Azure AI Content Safety (cloud-native, wrapped by LiteLLM)
install_tell: Azure AI Content Safety resource provisioned in customer Azure subscription; endpoint typically https://{resource}.cognitiveservices.azure.com or {resource}.contentsafety.cognitive.microsoft.com. Auth = Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header. API version pin (default 2024-09-01).
misconfig_patterns: Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key in LiteLLM .env on a publicly-readable box: same single-key blast radius as OpenAI moderation. Key rotates per-resource, not per-purpose.

AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 10000 hardcoded in the wrapper. Text-splitter chunks at word boundaries; an attacker who knows the chunking boundary can craft payloads that are benign per-chunk but malicious in aggregate (cross-chunk policy evasion).
API version pin 2024-09-01 default: operators who never override get whatever Microsoft retires next; surface migrations sometimes change response shape and silently break the parsing path.

Cross-reference: microsoft-purview is a SIBLING surface under the same Microsoft umbrella but a different product (Purview = governance/DLP, Content Safety = realtime moderation). Slice A's microsoft-purview.json covers Purview; this entry covers Content Safety.

passive: ssl.cert.subject.cn pivot identifies the Azure tenant but not the operator

active_probe.false_positive_check: Status-code-alone is identity-not-auth-state; 401 confirms resource exists; 404 = wrong resource path.

deployment_tells: Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header in client traffic (visible in misconfigured browser SPAs)
api-version query parameter is mandatory and a Microsoft-API tell
pivot_paths: Cert-pivot ssl.cert.subject.cn finds the resource name; resource name + leaked subscription key = full content-safety API access.
SPA bundles that embed Content Safety calls directly (instead of going through a backend) leak the subscription key; trivial to grep public GitHub for Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key + contentsafety.
LiteLLM wrapper inherits the same CVE chain as Bedrock/OpenAI wrappers.

added_surface: 10K-character chunking logic introduces a cross-chunk evasion vector that direct API callers do not have (direct callers handle their own splitting).
LiteLLM /guardrails/list discloses the content-safety guardrail presence and config name.
litellm_wrapper_delta.verdict: Mostly transparent at the API contract (same /contentsafety/text:* endpoints, same auth header). LiteLLM adds chunking (new evasion surface) and credential centralization. The cloud API itself is unchanged.

disclosure_contact.channel_observed: secure@microsoft.com / MSRC (cloud vendor; sibling to microsoft-purview)
